Old Moy's tower houses in 3D

The well town, every house built from its kit at true size: stone bases, the oldest on battered earth round the first well, brick storeys banded in white gypsum, parapets with horned corners, wind towers turned to the west wind. The courtyards in the middle of each block and the passages into them, the timber ramps of the roof route, and Cinema Square with the capped first well under its old ghaf. Drawn from the plan data, with the hero from the game for scale.

One of each kind

The Reese–Miller house on its battered earth base with rounded corners; a stone-based house of the Old High Street; and the later pencil infill, tiled and plumb with a lift. Every piece is built from the schedule below: SuperEggs, cut where they meet and capped. Open the doors and shutters to see a pair come apart; show the cuts to see every cut face; cut the houses open to see the walls thin as they rise and the ramp core, which this package does not build.

The kit's numbers

From CityPlan.TOWER_HOUSE, in metres. The plan's checks hold them together: five earth lifts make a storey, the core fits inside earth walls, holds are never more than m apart up a brick face.

Collision

Every house is solid to its outline. The landings are the plinth, the cornice, string courses, sills, kishk tops, parapets, the roof, the kiosk and manzar roofs and the wind tower's cap. Lattice, relief panels and drainpipes are decorative.

The courts are open to the sky and each has a way out at ground level, by a passage through a house or straight onto a road. The slots too small to be courts are built up solid to their lowest neighbour's roof, so nothing in the quarter is a pit with no way out.

No text

No sign is lettered. A house is known by its painted mark over the door, its frieze and its parapet. Nothing points to the passages or the ramps: a lit doorway at the back of a court, a timber ramp catching the evening sun.
